speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with neck and arm pain, paresthesias, and muscle weakness; to begin my assessment, could you tell me how long you have been experiencing these symptoms and what specific movements or positions seem to trigger the pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy with Radiculopathy.

The chronic burning pain, paresthesias, and progressive bilateral hand weakness in a 58-year-old male with significant comorbidities are classic signs of cervical spine pathology. Given the one-year duration and recent worsening, we must urgently evaluate for cervical spinal stenosis or myelopathy. REQUEST IMAGES: Cervical_Spine_MRI. REQUEST TEST: EMG/Nerve_Conduction_Study.
